notes: Units: seconds from time zero; bus numbers start at 1. At equal timestamps, mandatory arrivals and completions precede listed manual actions, then one automatic decision batch, then door starts and departures. Cutoff includes arrivals at that timestamp, cancels later demand and ends new automatic decisions. The temporal control window is start inclusive, end exclusive; its automatic components restore normal service at end. Manual bounded instructions may finish or expire during drain. Cohort includes all present just before its boundary plus births through cutoff, retaining original whole-journey clocks. until_recovered uses forward gap at most 110% of ideal; a convoy leader owns the long wrap arc. Stopping precedes overhead and sequential door service; both overlap holds. Starting extends the following travel segment after service/holds. True bypasses incur neither stopping nor starting penalties. A boarding_limit permits the specified number of new boardings per visit; existing boarding finishes. See scenario-guide.html for bounds and definitions.
name: Announced skips · six-stop lead-in
description: 12 stops, 4 buses, 40-second segments, fixed arrivals at 3 passengers per stop per minute, four-stop rides, and 5-second stopping and starting delays. Hold Bus 1 for 60 seconds at minute 20. At minute 25, Bus 1 announces six normally served future locations, followed by 12 locations serving every third stop, with an 1800-second cap from announcement. Boarding immediately respects the future pattern and all accepted drop-offs remain protected. The long lead-in really does bypass stops, but it starts too late to recover the default run and increases passenger time. Use this as a tradeoff lesson, then compare Recover with short announced skips.
